missions.title: Double Threat
missions.story: Captain Singh is nailing names to the performance board. "I want the bowlers who did it all in one spell: took at least two wickets AND kept the economy below eight. How many spells in this log qualify?"
missions.task: Wickets are in column F and economy in column G, rows 2 to 61. Write a COUNTIFS formula that counts spells where wickets >= 2 AND economy < 8. Both conditions must be true at the same time.
hints: COUNTIFS applies several filters at the same time. Each filter is a range followed by its condition, written as pairs.
Each pair is: the column to check, then the condition in quotes. Add a second pair for the second column.
Structure: =COUNTIFS(wickets_range, condition_for_wickets, economy_range, condition_for_economy). Point each range at the right column and write the threshold in quotes.

missions.title: When Wickets Cost
missions.story: Analyst Priya is studying Ujwal's impact. "When he takes wickets he clearly works hard, but I want to see the run cost. Add up every run Ujwal Mojidra gave away in spells where he also took at least one wicket."
missions.task: Runs are in column E, bowler names in column B, wickets in column F, rows 2 to 61. Write a SUMIFS formula: sum column E where column B equals "Ujwal Mojidra" and column F is >= 1.
hints: SUMIFS totals one column but only includes rows where every condition you set is true.
Put the column to sum first, then add condition pairs. You need two pairs here: one for the bowler name and one for the wicket count.
Structure: =SUMIFS(sum_range, bowler_range, "Ujwal Mojidra", wickets_range, ">=1"). Column E is the run tally; the other two columns provide the filters.

missions.title: Red or Green Light
missions.story: Selector Mehta runs a strict two-colour system. "Under eight runs per over is a green light. Eight or above is a red light. Look at Ujwal's very first spell in this log and write a formula for cell H2 that gives me a green light as a one and a red light as a zero."
missions.task: Economy is in column G. Write an IF formula for cell H2: if G2 is less than 8 return 1, otherwise return 0.
hints: IF has three parts separated by commas: the condition to test, the value to return when the condition is true, and the value to return when it is false.
Build the condition first: check whether the economy value in G2 clears the threshold the selector described.
Formula structure: =IF(condition, true_result, false_result). Replace the three pieces with what the selector wants to see.

missions.title: XP Bonus Calculator
missions.story: Manager Suresh runs the XP bonus scheme after every match. "Three wickets in a spell earns a hundred XP, two wickets earns seventy-five, one wicket earns fifty, and no wickets earns twenty-five. Write the formula for cell H2 so the board calculates Ujwal's bonus for his first spell automatically."
missions.task: Wickets for the first spell are in cell F2. Write an IFS formula for cell H2 that checks F2 = 3 (return 100), F2 = 2 (return 75), F2 = 1 (return 50), F2 = 0 (return 25). Cover all four cases.
hints: IFS tests conditions from left to right and returns the value paired with the first true condition.
Write one condition-value pair for each wicket count, starting with the highest count and working down to zero.
Structure: =IFS(cond_a, val_a, cond_b, val_b, cond_c, val_c, cond_d, val_d). Each condition checks F2 against a wicket count; the paired value is the XP from the manager's scheme.
